October 2026
We recently visited the new location and it's truly interesting, with a large, ample parking lot. I think they're missing a waiting room for exotic animals (I've only seen a waiting room for dogs and cats).

Since the clinic was acquired by a multinational, I've noticed a progressive decline in empathy, respect, and care for both patients and their owners, as well as a decline in professionalism, partly due to the frequent turnover of doctors.

After many years of entrusting my dogs to them, my latest experience was deeply disappointing.

I will look for a new facility where professionalism, respect, and empathy are still valued and where my dogs and I can feel in good hands.

I brought my cat Nana on September 28th after episodes of vomiting. I should point out that the cat had a heart condition but was regularly checked. The last check-up was in June, with ultrasounds and blood tests, and everything was normal. After the visit, they told me she had a kidney problem and the seriousness of the situation. They recommended hospitalization and that they would stabilize her. When I went to visit her, she was in a sort of closet. The next day, they called that Nana had died. I asked for explanations, but the doctor was very vague and couldn't tell me anything. She offered hypotheses, perhaps a blood clot. I mean, was she given an anticoagulant? Was she constantly monitored? Nana's rigor mortis was in an advanced stage, it couldn't have happened at 10:00 AM, and by 2:30 PM, she was already in the same state they gave her back to me. Now, I knew it could happen given her condition, which, I repeat, was well managed with medication. The doctor who took her in told me we'd call her any time. I said, if it were that serious, call me. I would have been thrown on the floor to hold her paw and pet her, to give her the love she's always had so she wouldn't feel alone in such a delicate moment. No! No call. I think the doctors weren't careful at all; they abandoned her unsupervised, they had very little empathy. I've been to various clinics for Nana, and she has overcome many very critical situations like the warrior she was. It was a very bad and painful experience, with little attention paid to these creatures. I'll never see her again.

The vets were very knowledgeable and kind, and were extremely helpful. I brought my Jackyina there on the night of October 26th at 4:00 AM because she couldn't give birth to her last puppy.
They resolved everything perfectly, performing a C-section on both mother and puppy, safe and sound.
HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

No thank you will ever be enough to express our gratitude to Dr. and surgeon Matteo Tomasi.
Our ginger cat, Whisky, arrived at the clinic with a complex, critical condition. A huge submandibular mass measuring approximately 6 x 3 cm, which had grown rapidly, was threatening his life. At the same time, however, the surgery posed significant risks as important anatomical areas were involved.
Despite this, Dr. Tomasi (who personally supported us throughout the entire process), in collaboration with Dr. Ettore Maggisano, completed the surgery with great success, and Whisky recovered in record time.
Throughout the process following the removal of the mass (which turned out to be a tumor) and its analysis, and throughout his convalescence, he kept us constantly updated, constantly interested in Whisky's health.
For this reason, we believe that, in addition to his technical professionalism, we were fortunate to find such a human doctor—a quality that truly makes the difference in difficult journeys like this.
Thanks again to the entire team, especially Dr. Tomasi, from our entire family.

No thank you will ever be enough to express our gratitude to Dr. Matteo Tomasi.
Our ginger cat, Whisky, arrived at the clinic in a complex and critical situation. A massive submandibular mass measuring approximately 6 x 3 cm, which had grown rapidly, was threatening his life. The surgery posed significant risks, as delicate and important anatomical areas were involved.
Despite this, Dr. Tomasi—who personally supported us throughout the entire process—in collaboration with Dr. Maggisano, completed the procedure with great success, and Whisky recovered in record time.
But what we want to emphasize is the extraordinary humanity and empathy of Dr. Tomasi, who immediately demonstrated his caring and kindness. THIS REVIEW IS WORTH LESS THAN ZERO. A VERY BAD EXPERIENCE. STRONGLY NOT RECOMMENDED. SERIOUS INEXPERIENCE.
IF YOU NEED TO HAVE A FAYETTE REMOVED OR AN X-RAY OR OTHER TRIVIAL THINGS, OK. BUT IF YOU NEED TO SEND YOUR DOG LONG-TERM CARE, RUN AWAY.
IN JULY I TOOK MY DOG IN WITH A SEVERE INFECTION, WHICH I THINK IS SEVERE.
I TOLD THE VETERINARIAN ON DUTY THAT HIS DEWICK'S CLASP HAD BROKEN OFF AND HIS ENTIRE LEGG IS EXTREMELY SWOLLEN, ALL THE WAY UP TO HIS SHOULDER. I FURTHER TOLD HER: I'M NOT A VETERINARIAN, BUT I THINK IT'S AN INFECTION. SHE CHECKED HIM QUICKLY WITH TERRIBLE ANXIETY BECAUSE HE'S A MOLOSSOID DOG (WHICH MAY APPEAR TO BE IMPRESSIVE, BUT HE WAS THE BEST-BEHIND DOG IN THE WORLD, NEVER BITED ANYONE, NOT A DOG OR A PEOPLE). SHE SENT ME AWAY, TELLING ME NO, IT'S JUST INFLAMMATION. I'M THE VETERINARIAN HERE, AND I KNOW WHAT I'M DOING, AND THE BILL IS ABOUT 150 EUROS.
3 DAYS LATER I RETURN BECAUSE IT SWELLS EVEN MORE UP TO THE WHOLE NECK AND BELLY HERE I FIND ANOTHER MAN VETERINARIAN TERRIFIED OF MY DOG. AS SOON AS I ENTER THE ROOM FOR THE CHECK-UP, HIS SKIN BURST FROM WHICH A LOT OF BLOOD MIXED WITH PUS IS COMING OUT AND HE TELL ME WITH ANGER AND ARROGANCE: BUT CAN'T YOU SEE THAT HE HAS AN INFECTION, ALL THE PUS IS COMING OUT. SO I GET ANNOYED AND TELL HIM I HAD ALREADY TOLD YOUR COLLEAGUE THREE DAYS AGO BUT SHE TOLD ME THAT IT WAS JUST INFLAMMATION. YOU SEE NOW AND HE TELL ME JUSTIFYING IT, YOU CAN OBVIOUSLY SEE THAT THE INFECTION COULD NOT BE SEEN YET. SO HE DOES THE TESTS WHICH RESULT IN A STRONG INFECTION. HE GIVES ME THE TREATMENT AND SENDS ME ANOTHER BILL OF APPROXIMATELY 270 EUROS. WE TAKE THE REQUIRED TREATMENTS, 20 DAYS PASS AND THE PROBLEM IS RESOLVED WITHOUT EVER UNDERSTANDING THE CAUSE OF THE INFECTION.
TOWARDS THE END OF AUGUST, WE NOTICED SEVERE BREATHING IN OUR DOG. WE REPORTED HIM TO THEY. THEY DID SEE THE TESTS, AND THEY DISPLAYED SEVERE ANEMIA, VERY LOW RED CELL COUNTS, AND THEY TOLD US IT COULD BE AN AUTOIMMUNE DISEASE OR LESHMANIA. WE ALSO REQUESTED THEM TO BE TESTED IMMEDIATELY FOR LESHMANIA. THE NEXT DAY IT WAS POSITIVE AND IN A VERY ADVANCED STAGE. THEY GIVE US THE TREATMENT, TELL US THAT IT WON'T BE VERY EASY TO SAVE HIM, BUT THEY WILL TRY.
I'M STOPING HERE BECAUSE I WANT TO MAKE A PREFACE. IN JULY, THE DEWICK'S NAIL WAS MUCH LONGER THAN NORMAL, LIKE THE REST OF THE NAILS. THERE WAS A STRONGER INFECTION, EVEN THAT WAS RECOGNIZED 3 DAYS LATER. PLUS, A LOT OF HAIR LOSS AND DANDRUFF.
THESE ARE ALL SIGNS OF POSSIBLE LEISHMANIASIS, BUT NO ONE HAS RECOGNIZED THESE WARNING SIGNS. IF THIS IS NOT INEXPERIENCE AND INCOMPETENCE, AS YOU CAN CALL IT.
NOW FOR THE REST,
WE CONTINUE WITH THE TREATMENT FOR LEISHMANIASIS, BUT IT IS GETTING WORSE AND WORSE, GETTING TO THE POINT WHERE OUR LIFE HAS STOPPED TOGETHER WITH THAT OF OUR GUY. LITTLE DOG, NOW TELL ME WHAT SHOULD I DO?
I'VE SPENT ALMOST 1,800 EUROS IN ALL SINCE JULY. THEY WANTED A HEAVY DEPOSIT FOR THE LAST STORAGE WHERE OUR DOG DIED. THEY ARROGANTLY ASKED US FOR IT, AND TODAY, EVEN THOUGH HE DIED, THEY WANTED US TO PAY FOR EVERYTHING.

YESTERDAY EVENING HE WAS NOT WELL, BUT I WOKEN UP CLEARLY AND RECOVERED WITH A GREAT DESIRE TO LIVE. SO MUCH SO THAT WHEN I LEFT THERE, HE JUMPED UP TO COME WITH ME, BUT OBVIOUSLY WE STOPPED HIM, AND THIS MORNING HE LEFT US FOREVER. THIS MORNING THEY TOLD US YOU DID THE RIGHT THING TO COME. THE DOG IS DYING SO DIRECTLY WITHOUT A LITTLE COMMON SENSE. THEY TOLD US TO GET THE INJECTION BECAUSE HE WOULD SUFFER, BUT YESTERDAY HE WASN'T LIKE THAT.
THEY JUST WANT MONEY. THEY ARE NOT ANIMALS, JUST NUMBERS. THEY ARE ALSO ARROGANT AND RUDE. HEARTLESS AND INEXPERIENCED. OBVIOUSLY, NOT ALL OF THE DOCTORS AND NURSES WERE ANGELS. BUT THERE ARE ONLY A FEW GOOD ONES.

An extremely negative experience after more than 10 years of trust.

I went to the Borghesiana Clinic with my 15-year-old dog, who had spent the night vomiting. Already that morning, he was showing very obvious neurological symptoms: a crooked face, eyebrow twitching, a tilted head, loss of balance, and difficulty walking.

Despite this, I was diagnosed with gastritis, attributing the instability to dehydration, and we were sent home with treatment and a syrup.

Dr. Francesca Mandetta had prescribed a dosage of 3 ml, but later, at the specialized veterinary center, I was told that the correct dose for my dog's weight was 2 ml.

The next day, the dog continued to worsen: he couldn't stand, he was swaying, he was shaking, and above all, he wasn't eating. I called the clinic again and was told to wait for the syrup to take effect.

After three days without food, I decided to take him to a specialized veterinary center on Nomentana (CVS), where, after further tests, ischemia was diagnosed.

What shocks me is that the neurological symptoms were already present during the first visit, but they weren't recognized and addressed. In a situation like this, I would have expected the priority to be understanding what was really happening to my dog, not discussing non-urgent visits like a dentist.

I urge anyone who turns to this facility to be very careful about which veterinarian they come across. My experience was that my dog's real problem wasn't recognized in time. I was truly afraid of losing him.

After more than 10 years of trust, I'm sorry to say, but I had the strong feeling that financial considerations came before the animal's real needs, with more attention paid to medications, visits, and services than to understanding the real problem.

I strongly advise against this clinic. I sincerely hope my little one recovers. ❤️‍🩹

We brought our cat because we found her in pain when we got home and foaming at the mouth. I left after an hour with a €300 deposit already paid and the doctor's promise to let us know how the cat was doing the next morning. The next morning we called to check in, and the staff's rudeness was ridiculous. We then went in the afternoon to check in and speak with the doctors.
Result:
- They would have kept the cat for further tests (thousands of euros)
- Medical tests and a neurological examination performed without any answers to the possible causes
- Pharmacy given at random for a supposed anti-epilepsy medication to be taken chronically for life
- €600 spent without any diagnosis, just pure hypotheses that I or chatGPT could have made
In essence, I took the cat away, tapered her off the anti-epileptic medication, and for over a month now she's been completely fine as before.
In short, it really seems like the clinic's staff's goal, rather than treating the animals, is to make the owners spend as much as possible, even using very subtle tactics like "if the cat dies, it's not our fault."

Obviously, this won't be the case for all employees. But the ones I've met have been like this.

THE CAT IS FINE, BUT NOT THANKS TO YOU!
